name: Joseph
overview: Joseph was a male member of the tribe of Levi, uniquely identified as the son of Shebaniah according to Nehemiah 12:14. He is noted among the priests who were descendants of Aaron, highlighting his role within the Levitical priesthood. This positions Joseph within a sacred lineage entrusted with priestly duties in Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Joseph, meaning 'he will add,' is a proper name recorded in Nehemiah 12:14. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it reflects a hopeful or providential meaning consistent with biblical naming traditions.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Joseph as the son of Shebaniah, as stated in Nehemiah 12:14. Beyond this father-son relationship, no additional family connections are documented in the provided facts.
scriptureSignificance: Joseph's significance lies in his priestly heritage as a descendant of Aaron, which underscores his role in the religious leadership of Israel. His identification in Nehemiah emphasizes the continuity of the Levitical priesthood after the exile. Although not the same Joseph renowned in Genesis, this Joseph's inclusion among the priests reflects the ongoing faithfulness of God's covenant people and their worship practices.
